newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says weak rand "great concern" to S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says weak rand "great concern" to S.Africa.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday that the country's weak rand currency was a source of great concern, but his cabinet ministers were addressing the issue.
"The depreciation of the rand is a source of great concern," Mandela said in an address to businessmen.
He said numerous reasons had been given for the fall, including that the rand was overvalued and the dollar had strengthened against a whole basket of currencies.

He said the International Monetary Fund offered South Africa funds to build foreign reserves, but that his deputy Thabo Mbeki, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and Trade Minister Alec Erwin, had said there was no reason to hurry.
"They said 'Let's not hurry. We are addressing the situation.'"
Mandela described Manuel as a conscientious and methodical person.
The rand has lost some 30 percent of its value against the dollar this year and was probing levels around 4.6850 to the U.S. unit at Wednesday's close.

It has recovered some ground this week from its worst ever level of 4.77, which it hit two weeks ago. But dealers said the currency remained vulnerable to further speculative attacks given the country's low reserves.
